mainTopic: The measures of the תודה loaves, the source for the size of the איפה, and שמואל's rule that measures may be raised by at most a sixth
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's math for the forty loaves of the תודה. In the wilderness measure the flour is twenty עשרונים, and in the Jerusalem measure it is thirty קבין. The גמרא asks how we know an איפה holds three סאין. רב חסדא learns it from a פסוק in יחזקאל that makes the איפה equal to the בת. A first attempt to prove the size of the בת fails, because we do not know the size of a חומר. A second פסוק works instead: ten בתים make a כור, which is thirty סאין. Then שמואל rules that measures, coins and profits may not be raised by more than a sixth. The גמרא tries three logical reasons for this rule and rejects each one. רב חסדא finally shows that שמואל learned it from a פסוק about the holy מנה, which was raised from 200 to 240. רבינא supports this from our משנה, where five Jerusalem סאין equal six wilderness סאין.

steps.title: Dividing the twenty tenths among the loaves
steps.stepSummary: The משנה splits the flour in the wilderness measure: ten עשרונים for the חמץ loaves and ten for the three kinds of מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten tenths go to the leavened loaves, one tenth per loaf. Ten tenths go to the מצה loaves. The מצה comes in three kinds: loaves, wafers, and scalded loaves. So each kind gets three and a third tenths, which works out to three loaves per tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its math for how the twenty עשרונים of flour are split among the forty loaves of the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are 10 חמץ loaves, so each one gets a full עשרון. The other 10 עשרונים are spread over 30 מצה loaves (10 of each kind). That gives 3⅓ עשרונים per kind and 3 loaves from each עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה; the basic dry measure for flour offerings
Regular (thick) מצה loaves
Thin מצה wafers
Loaves scalded or poached in hot water

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think each kind of מצה gets ten עשרונים. All thirty מצה loaves together share ten עשרונים.

phrases.english: Ten [tenths] for the leavened loaves:
a tenth per loaf,
and ten for the מצה loaves:
and among the מצה there are three kinds:
loaves, wafers, and scalded loaves.
So it comes out to three and a third tenths
for each and every kind,
and three loaves per tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's breakdown, which began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 10 עשרונים for 10 חמץ loaves; 10 עשרונים for 30 מצה loaves, so 3⅓ per kind and 3 loaves per עשרון.

steps.title: The same flour in the Jerusalem measure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה restates the division in Jerusalem קבין: thirty קבין in all, fifteen for חמץ and fifteen for מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the Jerusalem measure there were thirty קבין: fifteen for the leavened loaves and fifteen for the מצה. The fifteen for חמץ come to a קב and a half per loaf. The fifteen for מצה are split among loaves, wafers, and scalded loaves, so each kind gets five קבין, which is two loaves per קב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה does the same math again, this time using the larger Jerusalem measure, which counts in קבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thirty קבין split in half gives 15 for חמץ, so each of the 10 loaves gets 1½ קבין. The 15 for מצה are split among 3 kinds, giving 5 קבין per kind. Ten loaves from 5 קבין means 2 loaves per קב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jerusalem measure, which was larger than the earlier wilderness measure
A smaller dry measure; six קבין make a סאה

steps.whatToRemember: Same flour, two systems: 20 wilderness עשרונים equal 30 Jerusalem קבין. Each חמץ loaf is 1 עשרון, or 1½ קבין.

phrases.english: And in the Jerusalem measure
there were thirty קב,
fifteen for the leavened loaves
and fifteen for the מצה.
Fifteen for the leavened loaves:
a קב and a half per loaf;
fifteen for the מצה.
And among the מצה there are three kinds:
loaves, wafers, and scalded loaves.
So it comes out to five קבין
for each and every kind,
and two loaves per קב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same division as step 1, in the Jerusalem measure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 30 קבין: 15 for חמץ (1½ per loaf), 15 for מצה (5 per kind, 2 loaves per קב).

steps.title: Where do we learn the size of the measure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'five Jerusalem סאין' and asks for the source behind this measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The תודה came from five Jerusalem סאין. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting the משנה and asking for a source. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five Jerusalem סאין equal six wilderness סאין, which the משנה treats as two איפות. That only works if an איפה holds three סאין. The question is where that number comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
The thanks offering, brought together with forty loaves
A dry measure equal to six קבין
From where are these matters learned? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: גמרא:
The תודה would come
from five Jerusalem סאין.
From where are these matters learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the משנה's measurements
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that an איפה equals three סאין, which makes the משנה's measurements work

steps.title: רב חסדא: the איפה equals the בת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא cites יחזקאל: the איפה and the בת are one measure. Since a בת is three סאין, so is an איפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The פסוק says, 'The איפה and the בת shall be one measure.' Just as a בת is three סאין, so too an איפה is three סאין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by using a פסוק that makes the dry measure (איפה) equal to the liquid measure (בת).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the two measures. If we know the בת is three סאין, the איפה must be three סאין as well. This answer assumes we already know the size of the בת.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure for dry goods such as flour
A measure for liquids
One measure; the same size
Just as ... so too (a comparison pattern)

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole answer rests on knowing that the בת is three סאין. That is exactly what the גמרא questions next.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
As the verse says:
'The איפה and the בת
shall be of one measure.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 45:11. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: Just as a בת is three סאין,
so too an איפה is three סאין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יחזקאל equates the איפה with the בת, and a בת is three סאין, so an איפה is three סאין.

steps.title: How do we know the size of the בת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the בת itself is three סאין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the בת itself, how do we know its size?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב חסדא's answer depends on the בת being three סאין, so it asks where that is learned. This sets up the next attempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer that relies on an unproven assumption is not finished. The גמרא now needs a source for the size of the בת.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
From where do we learn it?

phrases.english: And the בת itself, from where do we learn [its size]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption behind רב חסדא's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a בת is three סאין

steps.title: Suggested source: the בת is a tenth of a חומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the size of the בת from the פסוק that calls it a tenth of a חומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learn it from what is written, 'that the בת may hold a tenth of the חומר'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: the פסוק says a בת is one tenth of a חומר. The challenge to this suggestion comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חומר is thirty סאין, a tenth of it is three סאין. That would give the size of the בת. The word אילימא tells us this idea is about to be knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
A large measure
A tenth part

phrases.english: If you say, from what is written:
'That the בת may hold a tenth of the חומר,'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, יחזקאל 45:11. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בת is a tenth of a חומר.

steps.title: But the איפה is also called a tenth of a חומר
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק calls the איפה a tenth of a חומר, so why would we need to learn the איפה from the בת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the איפה too, isn't it written, 'and the איפה a tenth of the חומר'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion: if the 'tenth of a חומר' wording teaches us the size, it would teach us the איפה directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'tenth of a חומר' were enough to give the size, רב חסדא would not need to compare the איפה to the בת at all. His comparison shows that this wording is not a usable source.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
A tenth

phrases.english: The איפה too, isn't it written:
'And the איפה a tenth of the חומר'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'a tenth of a חומר' gives the size of the בת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same wording is used for the איפה. If it worked, רב חסדא's comparison to the בת would be unnecessary.

steps.title: We don't know the חומר, so the suggestion fails
steps.stepSummary: The size of a חומר is unknown, so 'a tenth of a חומר' tells us nothing about either the איפה or the בת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, I don't know how much a חומר is. Here too, I don't know how much [the בת] is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the איפה could not be learned that way: we do not know the size of a חומר. That reason knocks out the suggested source for the בת too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tenth of an unknown amount is still unknown. So the 'tenth of a חומר' פסוק cannot give the size of the בת. The next step brings a different פסוק to answer the question of step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: I don't know how much
Here too (the same reasoning applies)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'tenth of a חומר' פסוק does not help, because the חומר's size is unknown. The next step gives the real source for the בת being three סאין.
steps.confusionAlert: The אלא here is not a new answer to the question about the בת. It explains why the suggested answer does not work.

phrases.english: Rather, a חומר, I don't know how much it is;
here too, I don't know how much [the בת] is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 7 and rejects the suggestion of step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects 'a tenth of a חומר' as the source for the size of the בת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The size of a חומר is unknown, so a tenth of it is also unknown.

steps.title: A new פסוק proves a בת is three סאין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from יחזקאל that says ten בתים make up a כור. Since a כור is thirty סאין, each בת is three סאין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from here: 'And the set portion of oil, the בת of oil, shall be a tenth of a בת from the כור, which is ten בתים, a חומר; for ten בתים are a חומר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier proof failed, so the גמרא brings a different פסוק to show that a בת is three סאין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old proof used 'a tenth of a חומר', which did not help because we did not know the size of a חומר. This פסוק ties the בת to the כור, and we already know a כור is thirty סאין. Ten בתים in a כור means each בת is three סאין, and an איפה is the same size as a בת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, learn it from here. This brings a new source after the old one was rejected.
A large measure of known size, equal to thirty סאין.
A liquid measure, the same size as an איפה.
Ten בתים, which together make up one כור.

steps.whatToRemember: A כור is thirty סאין and holds ten בתים, so a בת is three סאין. An איפה equals a בת, so an איפה is also three סאין.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And the set portion of oil, the בת of oil,
shall be a tenth of a בת from the כור,
which is ten בתים, a חומר;
for ten בתים are a חומר."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source that step 8 rejected with a new פסוק that links the בת to the כור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ten בתים make a כור, which is thirty סאין, so a בת is three סאין.

steps.title: שמואל limits increases to one-sixth
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that measures and coin values may not be raised by more than a sixth, and a seller may not profit by more than a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: We do not increase the measures by more than a sixth, nor the coin by more than a sixth, and one who makes a profit may not profit by more than a sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. שמואל gives three rules about how much things may be raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה described the measures being enlarged over time. שמואל sets a limit: a town that changes its standard measures, or the value of its coins, may not raise them by more than a sixth. A seller's profit is limited to a sixth in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: One-sixth.
Standard measures of volume.
A coin, or the value of a coin.
One who makes a profit from selling.

phrases.english: שמואל said:
We do not add to the measures
more than a sixth,
and not to the coin more than a sixth,
and one who profits may not profit
more than a sixth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל הַמִּדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the משנה's description of enlarging measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Measures, coin values and profits may be raised by up to a sixth, but not by more.

steps.title: What is the reason for the measures rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל forbids raising measures by more than a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's first rule. This sets up the attempts that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself is clear, but its basis is not. Why would a sixth be allowed and more than a sixth be forbidden? The next steps test possible answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind שמואל's rule in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the limit on raising measures is set at exactly one-sixth.

steps.title: Rising prices cannot be the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the rule exists to stop prices from rising, but rejects this because even a sixth would raise prices.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it drives up market prices, then if so, even a sixth should not be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reason, that bigger measures push prices up, and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry were higher prices, any increase would cause it, including an increase of exactly a sixth. Since שמואל allows a sixth, rising prices cannot explain where his line is drawn.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to test.
Driving up the market price.
If so. This introduces the problem with the suggestion.

phrases.english: If you say it is because of raising the market price,
phrases.notes: Literally 'breaking open the gate'. It means making market prices go up.

phrases.english: if so, even a sixth should also not be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 11 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects rising prices as the reason for שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An increase of a sixth would also raise prices, yet שמואל permits it.

steps.title: Perhaps the reason is אונאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the limit is about אונאה: up to a sixth keeps the sale from being cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of אונאה, so that there will not be a cancellation of the sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second reason. The limit of a sixth matches the rules of אונאה, so that sales are not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the laws of אונאה, a price that is off by more than a sixth lets the sale be cancelled. Keeping the change to a sixth or less means buyers cannot claim overcharging to undo their purchases. This explains why a sixth in particular is the line.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying in a sale.
Cancellation of the sale.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the types of אונאה: being off by exactly a sixth means the difference is returned, while more than a sixth lets the whole sale be cancelled.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of overcharging,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֶיהֱוֵי בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח,
phrases.english: so that there will not be a cancellation of the sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from step 12 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The one-sixth limit matches אונאה, so that sales are not cancelled.

steps.title: רבא: measured items can be returned for any shortfall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the אונאה reason with רבא's rule: anything sold by measure, weight or number can be returned even if it is off by less than a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said: anything sold by measure, by weight or by number, even if it is off by less than the amount of אונאה, the sale is reversed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the אונאה reason using a rule of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit of a sixth only applies when the value is a matter of estimating. Measures are exact, so according to רבא any difference at all reverses the deal. If measures were changed by even less than a sixth, sales could still be undone, so the אונאה reason does not explain שמואל's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely. This introduces a challenge from a known teaching.
Measure, weight and number: exact ways of selling.
Less than the amount of אונאה, meaning less than a sixth.
The sale is reversed, or the money is returned.

steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks out the אונאה reason. The גמרא tries another reason in the next step, and step 17 finally gives the real source for שמואל's rule.

phrases.english: But didn't רבא say:
anything sold by measure,
or by weight, or by number,
even if it is less than the amount of overcharging, the sale is reversed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the אונאה reason offered in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 13 that the one-sixth limit is based on the אונאה threshold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Measures are exact, so any shortfall reverses the sale. The one-sixth threshold of אונאה does not apply to them and cannot explain שמואל's limit.

steps.title: A new reason: protecting the merchant from loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the sixth limit protects a merchant (תגרא) from losing money when the measures change.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the rule is for the merchant's sake, so that he will not suffer a loss.
steps.whatsHappening: After the אונאה reason was challenged, the גמרא offers a new reason. The limit protects the merchant so he does not lose money if measures are raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A merchant who doesn't hear about a new, larger measure might keep selling by the old one. A merchant usually earns about a sixth, so a raise of up to a sixth only eats his profit and never puts him at a real loss.

keyTerms.meaning: A merchant or trader
A loss or damage
That it should reach him (happen to him)

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of the merchant,
so that a loss will not reach him.
phrases.notes: He means a merchant who didn't hear about the bigger new measure and keeps selling by the old one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the אונאה reason, which was challenged in step 14, with a new reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sixth limit makes sure a merchant selling by the old measure loses at most his profit, not his own money.

steps.title: Rejected: a merchant needs a profit, not just to avoid loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the merchant reason, because a merchant who only breaks even isn't really a merchant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the only goal that he not lose? Doesn't he need a profit? If someone buys and sells with no profit, is he called a merchant?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the merchant reason from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under that reason, a raise of a full sixth would wipe out the merchant's whole profit. If the rule were made to protect merchants, it should leave them some profit. So that reason cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Profit
Buy and sell (trading with no gain)
Is called

phrases.english: Is it only a loss that should not reach him?
Doesn't he need a profit?
Buy and sell [with no gain], is that called a merchant?!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיָאנָה הוּא דְּלָא לִימְטְיֵיהּ, רְוָחָא לָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the merchant reason given in step 15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A rule meant to protect merchants would leave them a profit, not just save them from loss.

steps.title: רב חסדא: שמואל learned it from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says שמואל's rule doesn't come from logic at all. It comes from a פסוק in יחזקאל about the מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: שמואל found a פסוק and taught from it: 'The שקל shall be twenty גרה; twenty שקלים, twenty-five שקלים, fifteen שקלים shall be your מנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: After all the logical reasons failed, רב חסדא gives a source from a פסוק. This step quotes the פסוק and sets up the next step, where its numbers are worked out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists 20 + 25 + 15 שקלים as one מנה, which adds up to 60 שקלים. The rule will come from these unusual numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק (verse)
Explained it and drew a teaching from it
A coin and weight; one שקל equals four דינרים
A small unit; twenty make a שקל
A larger unit; normally 100 דינרים (25 שקלים)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
Shmuel found a verse and expounded it:
"And the shekel shall be twenty gera;
twenty shekels, five and twenty shekels,
ten and five shekels,
shall be your maneh."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שְׁמוּאֵל קְרָא אַשְׁכַּח וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical reasons failed, gives a source from a פסוק instead.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's rule comes from the numbers in יחזקאל 45:12.
steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the סוגיא from guessing at reasons to a source text, which explains the exact 'sixth' amount.

steps.title: The problem: the פסוק's מנה comes to 240 דינרים
steps.stepSummary: Read simply, the פסוק makes a מנה equal 240 דינרים, but a מנה is normally only 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מנה would then be two hundred and forty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the פסוק's numbers don't match the normal מנה. This sets up the three lessons in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 60 שקלים times 4 דינרים each is 240 דינרים. A normal מנה is 100 דינרים, so the פסוק can't just mean an ordinary מנה. Something must be learned from the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hundred and forty
They come to / would be
A silver coin; four make one שקל

phrases.english: A maneh would be two hundred and forty!
phrases.notes: That's 60 שקלים × 4 דינרים each, but a regular מנה is only 100 דינרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a difficulty with the simple meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the פסוק's total for a מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's total (240 דינרים) contradicts the known value of a מנה (100 דינרים).

steps.title: Three lessons from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The extra amount teaches that the holy מנה was double, that measures may be raised by up to a sixth, and that the sixth is counted from the final total.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn three things from it: the holy מנה was doubled; we may add to measures but not more than a sixth; and the sixth is counted from the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the 240 problem by drawing three lessons from it. The second lesson is שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A holy מנה is double, so 200 דינרים. The פסוק adds 40 more to get 240, and 40 is exactly one sixth of 240. That shows a raise is allowed up to a sixth of the new total, which is one fifth of the old amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / conclude from it
The מנה used for holy matters
Doubled
One sixth
From the outside, meaning a sixth of the final total

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's sixth comes from יחזקאל: 200 became 240. The 40 added is a sixth of the final 240, which is a fifth of the original 200.
steps.confusionAlert: 'A sixth from the outside' does NOT mean adding a sixth of the old amount. It means the added part ends up as a sixth of the new total. That's the same as adding a fifth of the old amount (200 + 40).

phrases.english: Rather, learn three things from it:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה,
phrases.english: learn from it that the sacred maneh was doubled,
and learn from it that we may add to the measures
but may not add more than a sixth,
and learn from it that the sixth is from the outside.
phrases.notes: The 40 added is a sixth of the final 240, not a sixth of the old 200.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the 240 problem of step 18 by drawing three lessons from it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the extra amount is meant to teach something.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to contradict the known value of a מנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holy מנה = 200; adding 40 shows the most a measure may be raised: a sixth of the final total.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה about the תודה fits this
steps.stepSummary: רבינא shows that the משנה's 5 Jerusalem סאין = 6 wilderness סאין matches a sixth counted from the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Our משנה is also precise this way, for it teaches: the תודה came from five Jerusalem סאין, which are six wilderness סאין. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings support from our משנה for the idea that the sixth is counted from the final total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jerusalem סאה was enlarged, so 5 of them equal 6 of the old wilderness סאין. The added 1 is a sixth of the new 6 and a fifth of the old 5. That is exactly 'a sixth from the outside,' and the גמרא accepts the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Is precise; its wording proves the point
The thanks offering, brought with loaves
A measure of volume
The later, enlarged Jerusalem measures / the original measures from the time in the wilderness

steps.whatToRemember: Both the פסוק (200→240) and the משנה (5→6) show the same thing: a raise is allowed up to a sixth of the new total.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Our mishna is also precise this way,
for it teaches:
The thanks offering would come
from five Jerusalem se'ah,
which are six wilderness se'ah;
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third lesson of step 19 (the sixth is counted from the outside) from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The sixth is counted from the final total.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: the תודה came from five Jerusalem סאין, which equal six wilderness סאין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The גמרא accepts that the sixth is measured from the outside.
